question.text: Ganga Infra Trust, a Cat I AIF, credits INR 2.5 crore of interest income to its resident Indian LP, Mr. Rakesh Mehta (individual, PAN available), at the end of FY 2025-26. Under Section 194LBB, what is the TDS amount the AIF must withhold before distribution?

answer.text: Nil — no TDS applies to pass-through distributions.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 194LBB mandates that an Investment Fund deducts tax at 10% on ALL income (other than business income) distributed to a resident investor, regardless of the LP's own tax slab or the character of income. INR 2.5 crore x 10% = INR 25 lakh. Mr. Mehta will claim credit of this INR 25 lakh in his return and pay differential tax at his applicable slab rate (since interest is taxable at slab rates in his hands). The Trap: Option B is the 20% TDS rate that applies only to dividend distributions to NON-RESIDENT investors. Option C applies the individual slab rate — wrong because 194LBB is a flat 10% for residents irrespective of slab. Option D ignores that the Investment Fund must withhold on all pass-through income streams. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 194LBB computation including the NR branch (rate-in-force / DTAA). XIX-A tests it at the client-advisory angle — a distributor must explain to LPs why TDS appears even when their effective rate will differ. XXI-B (PMS) has no analogous TDS regime because PMS is a direct-custody model. Manager's Pro-Tip: As a Cat I Manager, automate the 194LBB withholding in your fund-accounting system and issue Form 64C by 30 June every year. LPs often chase you in July asking for tax credits — proactive delivery builds trust and reduces LP-service bandwidth drain during AGM season.
